summary: Session kernel retention is now bounded (Issue #76): RlmRuntimeImpl tracks kernelLastUse and evicts ready kernels idle past kernelIdleTtlMs (runtime-only knob, default 15 min, not in the GUI schema) at every eval admission. Active/settling kernels and keys with queued (not-yet-active) entries are never evicted; eviction uses kernel.dispose({keepCheckpoint:true}) so the committed M5 checkpoint survives and the next same-Session eval resumes through the documented recovery path, while a no-recovery runtime drops the namespace deterministically (fresh kernel, NameError).
steps: Verified at 5a1b6e1: kernels left the map only through reset, fatal teardown, or whole-runtime disposal, so every Session that ever called rlm_eval kept one Python process for the plugin lifetime.
Chose the idle-TTL policy over agent-lifecycle release because the runtime owns kernels by session key without an agent reference; M5/M10 recovery is the correct resume contract.
Dispose previously set retainCheckpoint=false (plugin-unload semantics), so the idle path opts in to keepCheckpoint:true to preserve the resume contract.

evidence.note: evicted session restores keep+1=42 with recovery.restored=true; no-recovery session sees NameError

limitations: Eviction is checked only on eval admission (no background timer); many-Session growth is bounded by usage patterns, not by an instantaneous cap.
